item.title: Feature Availability by Plan
item.description:
This page tells you which Layer5 Cloud capabilities each Layer5 plan includes. Your plan is one condition for using a capability, not the only one: your role and where your Layer5 Cloud deployment runs also decide what you can do. Those conditions follow the matrix and the limits table.

Plans 🔗

The matrix has one column for each of the four Layer5 plans: Free, Team Designer, Team Operator, and Enterprise. Each plan is offered with monthly and annual billing. The Free plan is the plan that Layer5 Cloud calls Personal in its plan records, so you see that name in subscription and entitlement data. Entitlements follow your organization’s plan. Current pricing and plan details are listed at layer5.io/pricing.

item.title: Feature Availability by Plan
item.description:
This page tells you which Kanvas capabilities each Layer5 plan includes. Your plan is the first condition for using a capability, not the only one: your role, your provider, and where you run Kanvas also decide what you can do. Those conditions follow the matrix.

Plans 🔗

The matrix has one column for each of the four Layer5 plans: Free, Team Designer, Team Operator, and Enterprise. Entitlements follow your organization’s plan. Current pricing and plan details are listed at layer5.io/pricing.

item.title: Permissions by Role
item.description:
This page tells you which Kanvas actions require a permission, which default roles grant each permission, and which actions are limited by something other than a permission. Use it to find out why an action is missing for a user and which role grants it.

How permissions work 🔗

A permission is a named key, such as Deploy Design, that allows one action. Keys are grouped into keychains, and a role bundles one or more keychains. Your organization assigns roles to users. Before Kanvas offers certain actions, it checks whether the user holds the matching key. Kanvas uses the shared Layer5 permission set and defines no permissions of its own. See Roles and Keychains.

item.title: Roles and Permissions
item.description:
This page tells you which permissions each default Layer5 Cloud role holds. Use it to find out why an action is missing for a user and which role grants it. For how roles, keychains, and permissions fit together, see Roles.

How permission checks work 🔗

A permission is a named key that allows one action, such as Create Team. A keychain groups keys, and a role groups keychains. Layer5 Cloud checks the key, never the role name. Before it runs a guarded action, Cloud resolves the organization the request names, then checks whether the user holds the key through a role in that organization. A user’s permissions are the union of the keys from every role the user holds there.

item.title: Security Reference
item.description:
This page states how keys, keychains, tokens, and sessions behave, exactly, as of Layer5 Cloud v1.0.278. For the model, read the Keys, Keychains, Sessions, and Tokens concepts. For tasks, use the security guides. For base URL, authentication, and the organization header, see the Cloud API. All paths below sit under /api unless noted.

Permission keys 🔗

Provider Admin holds every key. The table lists the default holders of the other roles. “Interface” means the control or tab is disabled or replaced by a permission error screen. “Server” means the Layer5 Cloud server refuses the request with HTTP 403.

item.title: Workspace and Environment Reference
item.description:
This page states how workspaces and environments behave, exactly. For the model, read the Workspaces and Environments concepts. For tasks, use the workspace guides. For every endpoint’s schema, see the REST API Reference, and for base URL and authentication see the Cloud API. All paths below sit under /api.

Fields, defaults, and limits 🔗

Property Workspace Environment
Name Up to 255 characters. Not required or unique on the API. Up to 255 characters. Not required or unique on the API.
Description Up to 255 characters. May be empty. Up to 255 characters. May be empty.
Organization Required on create. Fixed for the life of the workspace. Required on create (organizationId is required). Fixed for the life of the environment.
Owner The user who created it. Not recorded on create.
Starting state No teams, environments, designs, or views. No connections, in no workspace.
Kind Single kind. Ordinary when created through the API. Platform-provisioned environments exist and are protected.
Update Only the fields sent change. Name and description are both replaced; an omitted field becomes empty.
Plan check None. None. The feature matrix lists environments under Enterprise.
Count limits None. An organization must keep at least one workspace. None.

Layer5 Cloud creates My Workspace in any organization that has no workspace.

item.title: Cloud API
item.description:
The Layer5 Cloud REST API lets you build integrations, retrieve data, and automate your infrastructure. This page states the conventions every endpoint shares: base URL, authentication, organization context, pagination, and errors. For the list of endpoints, see the REST API Reference.

Base URL 🔗

Every endpoint lives under /api on the host of your Layer5 Cloud deployment.

Deployment Base URL
Hosted Layer5 Cloud https://cloud.layer5.io/api
Self-hosted https://<your-cloud-host>/api

item.description:
These pages state what Layer5 Cloud does, exactly: which plan includes a capability, which role holds a permission, how to reach support, and how to call the REST API. Use them to check a fact. To learn how the pieces fit together, start with Concepts.

Page Use it to

item.title: Help and Support
item.description:
Kanvas gives you two ways to get help without leaving the canvas: the Help Center, a single place for documentation, learning material and community channels, and the support form, which sends a request to the Layer5 team. This page lists what each one contains, which support channels each plan includes, and the conditions the support form needs to work.

Help Center 🔗

The Help Center is a dialog with eight entries. Open it from the canvas context menu or from the help control in the whiteboard dock. It also opens from the Get Help action in the troubleshooting panel.
